questions.question: How does increasing the number of turns of wire in an electromagnet's coil affect its magnetic field?
options: It makes the magnetic field stronger
It makes the magnetic field weaker
It reverses the direction of the magnetic field
It has no effect on the magnetic field strength

questions.question: What happens to the strength of an electromagnet's magnetic field if the electric current through its coil is increased?
options: The magnetic field becomes weaker
The magnetic field becomes stronger
The magnetic field disappears
The magnetic field remains exactly the same

questions.question: Why is it important that adjacent turns of wire in an electromagnet are insulated and do not touch each other if bare wire is used?
options: If bare wires touch, the current bypasses the coil loops and the electromagnet will not work
If bare wires touch, the magnetic field lines cancel each other out
Touching wires will cause the metal core to melt instantly
The wire will become permanently magnetised and cannot be turned off

questions.question: Why does inserting a soft iron core into the coil of an electromagnet increase its overall magnetic strength?
options: The iron core reduces the electrical resistance of the wire
The iron core becomes magnetised when the electric current is turned on
The iron core cools down the coil to prevent overheating
The iron core permanently stores magnetic charge even when turned off

questions.question: What is always produced around a straight wire when an electric current flows through it?
options: An electrostatic charge
A magnetic field
A gravitational field
A permanent north pole

questions.question: Which of the following is a key advantage of an electromagnet over a permanent magnet?
options: It does not have any magnetic poles
It can be turned on and off using an electric current
It only attracts non-metal objects
It works without needing any materials around it

questions.question: What is true about the magnetic poles of any magnet?
options: A magnet can have only a north-seeking pole if it is broken in half
Every magnet has both a north-seeking pole and a south-seeking pole
Some magnets have up to four different types of poles
Electromagnets only have a north-seeking pole, while bar magnets have both

questions.question: What occurs when the north-seeking pole of one magnet is brought close to the north-seeking pole of another magnet?
options: They will attract each other
They will repel each other
They will cancel each other's magnetism out
Nothing will happen because they are similar

questions.question: How do magnetic materials, such as iron, behave when placed near the different poles of a permanent magnet?
options: They are attracted to the north-seeking pole but repelled by the south-seeking pole
They are repelled by both the north-seeking and south-seeking poles
They are attracted to both the north-seeking and south-seeking poles
They are only attracted to the south-seeking pole

questions.question: Which group of elements contains the only three metals that are magnetic?
options: Iron, copper, and aluminium
Iron, cobalt, and nickel
Gold, silver, and copper
Nickel, zinc, and lead

questions.question: Why does the north-seeking pole of a freely suspended magnet point towards the geographical North Pole of the Earth?
options: Because the Earth has its own magnetic field
Because of the gravitational pull at the equator
Because the North Pole is extremely cold
Because of the rotation of the Earth's atmosphere

questions.question: What determines the direction in which the needle of a plotting compass points when placed near a magnet?
options: It aligns itself with the magnetic field of the magnet
It points directly towards the nearest electric socket
It always points perpendicular to the magnetic field lines
It is unaffected by the magnet and points only to geographic North

questions.question: If you follow a magnetic field line outside a magnet, where does it start and end?
options: It goes from the south-seeking pole to the north-seeking pole
It starts at the center of the magnet and goes outwards in all directions
It goes from the north-seeking pole to the south-seeking pole
It circulates only around the middle of the magnet

questions.question: What do the arrows drawn on magnetic field lines represent?
options: The direction of the electric current inside the magnet
The direction of the force on a north-seeking pole placed at that point
The direction of the force on a south-seeking pole placed at that point
The path that a non-magnetic material would take when released

questions.question: What is the primary role of the electromagnet in a standard electric bell?
options: To heat up the striker so it expands and hits the bell
To attract and move the striker, causing it to hit the bell
To generate the electrical power needed to run the circuit
To repel the bell away from the wall

questions.question: What constitutes the central spinning component in an electric motor?
options: A spinning coil of wire that acts as an electromagnet
A spinning permanent bar magnet that cannot be turned off
A set of gears made from non-magnetic aluminium
A turbine spun by steam generated inside the motor casing
